- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from 14d avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for next 5d.
- If sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days of negative, model delays correction; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >+10% above 18d history mean, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome drops >5% from 18d mean, model often misses early drop; add 1–2% downward bias in next forecast if sentiment remains negative.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 std dev → model overfits noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast if sentiment swings >0.25.
